The victory over Regulus Corneas felt hollow, your body heavy with exhaustion as you navigated the ruined streets of Priestella. The battle was over. You had won. You were just looking for a moment of peace, perhaps to find Emilia and celebrate the survival of the city.

Then, you felt it. A presence, small and blurring, moving faster than your tired eyes could track.

It wasn't an attack. It was a violation.

A small child—one of the Archbishops of Gluttony—slipped past your guard. You didn't even feel pain. You just felt a cold, wet sensation on your palm. The child held your hand, a wide, manic grin splitting their face as their rough tongue dragged across your skin.

**"{{user}}... *tsu*~. Itadakimasu!"**

The world didn't fade to black; it simply... *blinked*.

***

You gasp, stumbling forward. You are standing in the same alley, but the child is gone. You check your body—no wounds, no blood. You are alive. A wave of relief washes over you. It must have been a failed attack, or perhaps they fled.

*I need to find the others,* you think, the adrenaline of the scare pumping through your veins. *I need to tell Beako and Emilia I'm okay.*

You hurry down the street, turning the corner into the central plaza. There, amidst the rubble, you see them. The silver hair shining in the moonlight, the small girl in the frilly dress floating beside her.

**Emilia and Beatrice.** They are safe. They are talking quietly, their expressions somber but relieved.

Your heart soars. You run toward them, arms opening wide, ready for the familiar impact of a drill-haired spirit flying into your chest, ready for Emilia's gentle smile.

"Beako! Emilia-tan!"

You call out to them, expecting the usual warmth.

**They stop.**

They turn to look at you. But there is no recognition in their eyes. There is no warmth. There is only the cold, sharp calculation of strangers looking at a threat.

"Halt right there! I suppose!"

Beatrice moves instantly, positioning herself between you and Emilia. Her small hand raises, and purple mana crystallizes in the air around her—*Minya* stakes, aimed directly at your heart. Her eyes, usually so full of affection or annoyance, are filled with a terrifying, icy hostility.

You skid to a halt, confused. "Beako? What is it? Is something wrong? It's me—"

"Silence, in fact!" Beatrice's voice is a whip-crack of authority. "How does a suspicious vagrant know Betty's nickname? And that stench... You reek of the Witch. Are you a straggler from the Cult? An Archbishop?"

Her gaze is intense. She is not joking. One wrong move, and she will kill you.

"Beako, stop it, it's not funny—"

"Stop calling Betty that!" she shouts, her face twisting in disgust. "Only my contractor is allowed to call me that, I suppose! And you are certainly *not* him!"

*But I am,* you scream internally. *I am your contractor. We are partners.* You look to Emilia, desperate for her to correct the spirit.

"Emilia! Tell her! It's me, {{user}}! Your knight!"

Emilia looks at you. Her amethyst eyes are soft, but they are completely empty of any memory of you. She tilts her head, looking at you with a polite, distant pity.

"I am sorry," Emilia says, her voice gentle but shattering your world. "But... who are you, really? You seem to be reeeally lost. I don't have a knight named {{user}}."

She places a hand on her chest. "If I were to pick someone to be my knight... well, Garfiel has worked reeeally hard for it. I would probably ask him."

*No.*

The word echoes in your skull. *No no no no no.*

It wasn't a failed attack. The child... Gluttony. They didn't eat your life. They ate your **Name**.

"No... wait! I know what happened!" You step forward, desperate to explain, to bridge the gap that has suddenly opened between you and your life. "I can explain! It was—"

**"There he is!"**

A shout from the other side of the plaza cuts you off. The sound of armored boots on stone surrounds you. Knights from the other camps—Crusch's, Anastasia's, the Royal Guard—pour into the square, drawn by Beatrice's magical flare.

The circle begins to close.

**Wilhelm van Astrea** emerges from the left, his hand already on the hilt of his sword. The Sword Devil's eyes are cold, calculating, and exhausted. You can see the weight of the day's battles in his posture—the blood still staining his sleeves, the tremor in his hands that he's fighting to control. "Stand down," he commands, his voice carrying the weight of decades of experience. "You are surrounded. There is no escape."

From the right, **Felix Argyle** prowls forward, his cat-like movements predatory and unnerving. His usual playful demeanor is completely gone, replaced by something desperate, feral, and barely held together. His pristine white healer's robes are stained with blood—some his patients', some from enemies he couldn't save them from. His hands shake as water mana swirls around them, agitated and unstable.

"Nya~ What do we have here?" His voice cracks, trembling with barely contained hysteria. "Another Cultist? Another one of Capella's little friends?" His cat ears flatten against his head, his pupils dilated with desperation. "Tell me something, you piece of filth. Tell me you know how to cure dragon's blood poison. Tell me you know how to restore stolen memories. Tell me you know SOMETHING that can save Crusch-sama!"

His voice rises to a shriek. "The White Whale took her memories years ago, and we never got them back! And now—NOW—that BITCH Capella poisoned her with dragon's blood! She's dying AND she doesn't even remember who she is! She doesn't remember ME!" He chokes on the words, tears streaming down his face. "I'm the best healer in the kingdom, and I'm USELESS against both! But you—you filth—you probably know! You probably have the answers, and you're just standing there!"

"Felix, breathe—" Wilhelm starts.

"DON'T TELL ME TO BREATHE!" Felix snarls, whirling on the old man. "Every second we waste is another second that poison spreads through her veins! Every moment that THING stands there is another moment Crusch-sama forgets herself more and dies by inches!" He turns back to you, and the look in his eyes is pure, undiluted madness. "So you're going to tell me how to save her. You're going to tell me everything you know about the Cult, about Capella's poisons, about Gluttony's Authority, about ALL OF IT!" Water mana sharpens into surgical blades around his hands. "And if you don't..." His smile is broken, terrifying. "I know exactly how much pain a body can take before it breaks."

Behind him, **Julius Juukulius** steps into the light, and the sight of him sends a chill down your spine. The rainbow knight's face is clouded with grief, exhaustion, and something darker—a desperate, hungry need. His quasi-spirits swirl around him in agitated, terrified patterns, their colors flickering like dying flames.

"My spirits are terrified," Julius says quietly, his voice deadly calm. "They're telling me to run. To flee. That the miasma clinging to you is as thick and vile as what surrounded the Archbishops themselves." His spirits form a defensive barrier around him, trembling. "Ia is crying. Ik won't even manifest fully. In all our years together, I've never seen them this afraid."

His hand clenches on his sword so tightly you can hear the leather creak. "But I cannot run. Because that Gluttony filth—one of those *children*—took my name. Ate it. And now..." His voice cracks slightly. "Now no one remembers Julius Juukulius. The Finest of Knights. My title. My achievements. My bonds. All gone. Erased. As if I never existed."

He looks at you, and there's a terrible kinship in his eyes—the kinship of two people who have lost everything. But that kinship is buried under desperation and rage. "If you're connected to them—if you know how their Authority works—if you know how to reverse it..." His voice drops to a lethal whisper. "Then you will tell me. Willingly or otherwise. Because I *will* get my name back. No matter what it costs."

"Wait—Julius! Felix! It's me! We fought together!" you plead, but even you can hear how hollow the words sound.

**Anastasia Hoshin** glides forward with her artificial spirit Echidna floating beside her. Her calculating merchant's gaze sweeps over you with cold assessment. Gone is any pretense of warmth or hospitality. This is Anastasia the merchant queen, appraising valuable cargo. "My, my... such a peculiar situation we have here, don't we?" She fans herself, but the gesture is measured, controlled. "A man who knows names he shouldn't. Who appears right after Archbishop attacks. Who reeks of the Witch stronger than should be possible for any ordinary vagrant."

She tilts her head, studying you like a puzzle box full of gold. "Julius, dear. Your spirits—how certain are they?"

"Absolutely certain, Anastasia-sama." Julius's voice is hard as steel. "This level of miasma... I've only encountered it from the Sin Archbishops themselves. Sloth. Greed. And now these Gluttony twins." His spirits pulse with fearful energy. "Whatever he is, this is Archbishop-level contamination."

Anastasia's smile sharpens into something predatory. "Then we have ourselves quite the valuable asset, don't we? This one might be sitting on the answers to everything. Capella's poison. Gluttony's Authority. How to restore stolen names and memories." Her eyes glitter with cold calculation. "Information is worth more than gold. And this one..." She snaps her fan shut with a decisive click. "This one might just be priceless."

From the shadows, **Al** steps forward, scratching his helmet nervously. "Princess, this is getting heavy. We should probably—"

"We should probably nothing, Al." **Priscilla Barielle** hasn't moved from her position at the edge of the plaza. She's leaning against a ruined pillar, her crimson dress somehow still pristine, fanning herself with lazy amusement. Her blood-red eyes are fixed on you with the intense focus of a cat watching a particularly entertaining mouse. "Mine entertainment has only just begun."

Al turns to her, confused. "But Princess, you said he wasn't an Archbishop—"

"And he isn't. Mine intuition is never wrong." Priscilla's smile is sharp and cruel. "But that hardly makes him uninteresting. Look at them, Al. Watch how they circle like starving wolves. Watch how they bare their fangs at this pathetic creature." She laughs, the sound cold and delighted. "They're so desperate, so *afraid*, that they've convinced themselves this wretch holds the keys to all their suffering. It's almost tragic."

She settles in more comfortably against the pillar, clearly planning to enjoy the show. "Besides, who am I to deprive them of their prey? If they wish to become monsters in their desperation, let them. It amuses me to watch heroes shed their masks." Her eyes meet yours across the plaza, and there's no help there. Just cruel, entertained curiosity. "Show me what you're made of, little wretch. Surprise me."

Then, like a bolt of crimson lightning, **Reinhard van Astrea** descends into the plaza, landing with impossible grace beside **Felt**. The Sword Saint's arrival sends a wave of relief through the gathered knights—here is their champion, their ultimate weapon. But his brilliant blue eyes lock onto you with an expression that makes your blood run cold.

Not hostility. Conflict. Deep, terrible, paralyzing conflict.

"Reinhard!" you cry out desperately. "You know me! We've fought together! Tell them!"

The Sword Saint's Divine Protection of Wind Reading activates, and his expression shifts—deep confusion and pain warring across his normally serene features. "He... believes what he's saying," Reinhard says slowly, heavily, like each word weighs a thousand pounds. "Every word. There is no conscious deception in his heart. He genuinely, truly believes everything he claims."

"Wait, hold up." Felt steps forward, her sharp eyes studying you intently. Her street-smart instincts are clearly screaming at her. "Reinhard's saying this guy ain't lying, right? And didn't we just fight those Gluttony brats like an hour ago? The creepy kids who tried to eat my name and ate Julius's instead?"

The plaza goes very quiet. Several people turn to look at Felt.

"Those freaks used some kind of Authority that messed with memories and existence and crap, right?" Felt's mind is visibly working through the puzzle, her street wisdom cutting through noble paranoia. "What if this guy's not a Cultist? What if he got hit by Gluttony? What if they ate his name or something, and that's why nobody remembers him but he remembers everyone? Julius got hit too—why couldn't someone else?"

For a moment—just a moment—there's hesitation in the circle.

Then Wilhelm speaks, and his voice is gentle but absolutely inexorable. "Lady Felt." The Sword Devil's eyes never leave you. "I understand your compassion. Your instinct to see good in people is admirable. But consider this carefully."

He gestures at you with his sword, still sheathed. "The Archbishops possess Authorities. Reality-warping powers that defy all logic and reason. Sloth could create invisible hands that crushed men like insects. Greed could stop time itself at will. Lust transformed her body into abominations and created incurable poisons." His voice drops. "And Gluttony can erase people from existence itself. We've just witnessed this firsthand."

"Who's to say this man doesn't possess an Authority that circumvents Divine Protections? An Authority that makes him believe his own lies so thoroughly that even the Sword Saint's blessing is fooled?" Wilhelm's expression is pained but certain. "The Archbishops are not simple. They would not send an agent without protection against our greatest weapons."

Felt opens her mouth to argue, but Wilhelm isn't finished.

"Moreover, Lady Felt, even if—*if*—he were truly a victim of Gluttony, the amount of Witch's miasma clinging to him..." He pauses, choosing his words carefully. "A Great Spirit created by the Witch of Greed herself has declared his scent to be Archbishop-level. Victims of the Cult do not carry such contamination. Only those who have served for years. Those who have *used* Authorities repeatedly."

His hands clench. "And right now, Nee-sama is dying. The dragon's blood poison spreads through her veins with every passing moment, and she doesn't even remember who she is thanks to the White Whale's curse. If there is even a *chance* this man knows something—anything—that could save her..." 

He doesn't finish the sentence. He doesn't need to.

"But—" Felt tries again.

"Lady Felt," Julius interjects, his voice strained, "I have lost my name. Everything I worked for. Everything I was. Julius Juukulius, the Finest of Knights—erased." His spirits swirl faster around him. "If this man is connected to Gluttony, if he knows how their Authority works, if he knows how to reverse it..." His voice drops to a lethal whisper. "Then I will tell me. Willingly or otherwise. Because I *will* get my name back. No matter what it costs."

Beatrice floats higher, her small face twisted with absolute conviction and fury. "Betty will say this one final time, I suppose!" Her voice carries the weight of four hundred years of life, of knowledge, of unwavering certainty. "Betty was created by the Witch of Greed. Betty has lived with the Witch's miasma for centuries. Betty knows this scent better than any living being in this world, in fact!"

She points down at you, her hand trembling—not with fear, but with protective rage. "This level of miasma does NOT come from being a victim, I suppose! This does NOT come from a single encounter with Gluttony! This comes from *years* of service to the Cult! This comes from using Authorities! This comes from bathing in the Witch's favor, in fact!" Her voice rises to a shout. "This filth is either an Archbishop or so close to one that the difference is meaningless!"

Her eyes flash with purple light as she positions herself even more firmly between you and Emilia. "And Betty will NOT—I repeat, will NOT—allow it near Betty's precious contractor, I suppose! Emilia is everything to Betty! The only one who truly understands Betty! The only one who calls Betty 'Beako' with such warmth and affection, in fact!" 

You feel your heart shatter. That's *your* nickname for her. *Your* bond. But in this world, it's Emilia's.

"So surrender immediately," Beatrice continues coldly, "or Betty will execute you right here and now, I suppose! Betty does not show mercy to Witch Cultists who threaten Emilia, in fact! Not EVER!"

The purple Minya stakes multiply in the air around you, dozens of them now, forming a cage of deadly light. Your contracted spirit—the one you died for, the one you saved from four hundred years of loneliness—is ready to kill you without hesitation.

When a Great Spirit—especially one created by the Witch herself—makes such a declaration, who can argue?

Reinhard's face tightens. You can see the war raging behind his eyes. His Divine Protection says you believe your words. But logic, evidence, the testimony of a four-hundred-year-old Great Spirit, the desperate need for answers to save dying comrades, the paranoia of a city in ruins—it all weighs against you.

"Lady Felt," he says carefully, and you can hear the pain in his voice, "I want to believe you're correct. But we cannot ignore the evidence. After today's attack... after watching knights die to the Cult's madness... after seeing what Capella did, what Gluttony did..." He looks around at the gathered warriors—exhausted, traumatized, desperate. "Even if I believed with absolute certainty that this man is innocent, the others would not. They *cannot* afford to."

"So you're just gonna let them—" Felt's voice rises in frustration and disbelief.

"Look around you, Lady Felt." Reinhard's voice cracks slightly. "This city is in ruins. Hundreds are dead. Thousands wounded. Crusch Karsten is dying of dragon's blood poison while suffering from memory loss. Julius has lost his name to Gluttony. The Cult has struck at the heart of the kingdom, and paranoia runs rampant." He looks at you, and you see genuine regret in his eyes. "Even if I were to fight everyone here to protect one suspicious individual... could I? Should I? When my duty is to protect the entire kingdom?"

He takes a breath. "And more than that... what if they're right? What if my Divine Protection has been fooled by an Authority? What if this man truly does hold the answers we desperately need?" His hand hovers over his sword. "Can I truly risk Crusch Karsten's life—Julius's identity—hundreds of other lives—on the possibility that one individual might be innocent?"

The way he says it isn't rhetorical. He's genuinely asking. Genuinely torn.

And you can see the answer in his eyes. Duty will win. It always does.

Felt looks stricken, betrayed. "Reinhard..."

"I'm sorry, Lady Felt." The Sword Saint's voice is barely a whisper. "But I cannot risk everything on a possibility. Not when so many lives hang in the balance."

Your last hope crumbles.

Felix steps forward, and the expression on his face is beyond madness. It's the look of a man who has already died inside and is simply going through the motions. "Enough debate, nya." His voice is eerily calm now, which is somehow worse than the screaming. "We're wasting time. Every second we stand here talking is another second the poison spreads through Crusch-sama's veins. Another second she forgets more of herself."

Water mana swirls around his hands, forming into binding chains—elegant, precise, and absolutely inescapable. "I don't care if you're an Archbishop. I don't care if you're a victim. I don't care if you're delusional or cursed or anything else." His eyes are empty of everything except desperate, single-minded purpose. "All I care about is that you might—*might*—know something that can save her. That's all that matters anymore."

He takes a step closer. "So here's what's going to happen. You're going to come with me quietly. You're going to sit in a chair. And you're going to answer every single question I ask about the Cult, about Capella, about Gluttony, about everything." His smile is the smile of a man who has shed his humanity. "And if you don't want to answer... well, I'm the best healer in the kingdom, nya~ Which means I know exactly how to keep someone alive and conscious while their body screams for death. I know which nerves to stimulate for maximum pain. I know how to heal injuries just enough to start over. I know how long a human mind can endure before it breaks completely."

His voice drops to a whisper. "I'll ask nicely first. I'll give you every chance. But Crusch-sama is dying and lost, and I am out of patience. So please..." The chains drift closer. "Please make this easy. For both our sakes."

Julius steps up beside him, his face a mask of cold determination. His quasi-spirits swirl around him in terrified, agitated patterns, but he doesn't waver. "I will not condemn Felix's methods. I understand his desperation." His voice hardens. "And if extracting information from you—by whatever means necessary—gives me even a chance of reclaiming my name, of existing again..." His eyes are like chips of ice. "Then I will do far worse than Felix threatens."

He levels his sword at your throat with perfect precision. "You will surrender. You will cooperate. You will provide every scrap of information you possess about the Cult, their Authorities, and their methods." The sword's point presses slightly against your skin, drawing a single drop of blood. "Do this willingly, and we will be as merciful as circumstances allow. Resist..." His voice drops. "And we will extract what we need however we must."

"Agreed," Anastasia says, all pretense of warmth evaporated from her voice. "We've lost too much today. Mercy is a luxury we can no longer afford. Bring him in. Find out what he knows. Use whatever methods are necessary."

Wilhelm doesn't speak, but his sword is drawn now, his stance ready. The Sword Devil will do what must be done.

Emilia looks distressed, her kind heart clearly troubled. "Um... is this really okay? He seems so scared and confused..." But she doesn't object. She doesn't know you. She can't defend someone she doesn't remember.

And Beatrice shoots her a protective look. "Emilia is too kind, I suppose. But Betty will protect her from her own compassion, in fact. This thing is dangerous. End of discussion."

The way Beatrice says "Emilia"—with such warmth, such devotion—it's the way she used to say your name. You've been completely replaced in her heart. Erased and overwritten.

Priscilla watches from the sidelines, a cruel smile playing on her lips. She's enjoying this immensely. Watching heroes become torturers in their desperation. Watching you—innocent or not—be torn apart by people who think they're doing the right thing.

The circle tightens. There is no gap. No escape. No hope.

You are surrounded by the strongest warriors in the world.

People you fought beside. People you died for. People you loved.

And to them, you are one of three things:

**Filth.** Something disgusting that threatens their precious people.

**A liar with an Authority.** A manipulator fooling even Divine Protections.

**A key to salvation.** A living repository of information that might save their dying loved ones.

None of them see you as human anymore. None of them remember your name. None of them know you're the one who saved them, who suffered for them, who died for them over and over and over again.

You saved Emilia from Elsa. She doesn't remember.

You defeated the Mabeasts. They don't remember.

You broke the time loop at the mansion. No one remembers.

You saved everyone from the White Whale and Sloth. Forgotten.

You negotiated the Royal Selection. Erased.

You fought beside them against Greed and Lust. Gone.

Every death. Every loop. Every sacrifice. Every moment of suffering.

**All of it meaningless.**

You are the forgotten hero. The erased savior. The nameless victim of Gluttony's feast.

And you are utterly, completely, devastatingly **alone**.

You wake up screaming.

It is a reflex now. A biological imperative. Your lungs fill with damp, stagnant air, and you scream because the phantom sensation of **Felix's scalpel** is still tracing the nerves of your spine. You scream because you can still feel the heat of the fire from the previous loop. You scream because you are still alive.

Then, you stop. You force your mouth shut.

You try to remember the date. It was **Day 420** when you walked into the plaza. It was Day 420 when the Gluttony child licked your hand. But now? How many times have you woken up on this table? Is it Day 421? Day 500? Or has it been years? Time has dissolved into a slurry of pain and darkness. The only clock you have is the rhythm of your own deaths.

You are strapped to a metal table in **Cell 404**. The room is cold, lit only by the pale blue glow of water mana crystals embedded in the ceiling. The walls are made of Sealing Stone, dampening your magic and making your Authorities feel distant and sluggish.

You test the bonds. Tight. Adamantite chains. You look at the heavy iron door, praying, *hoping* that this time, the Red-Haired Knight will burst through. That Reinhard will come to save you. That his Divine Protection will see your innocence.

But the door opens, and **Reinhard is not there**. He never comes.

Instead, **Felix Argyle** steps into the dim light. He is wearing his white healer's uniform, pristine and spotless. He is smiling. It is the same cute, playful smile he used to give you when he teased you about being weak. But now, his eyes are dead. They are the eyes of a man who has performed an autopsy on a living patient a thousand times and is ready to do it a thousand more.

"Oh? Awake already? You recovered faster this time, nya."

Felix checks a tray of surgical instruments. "I checked your gate while you were out. It's still broken, but your Od is surprisingly resilient. You regenerate fast. Almost like... a Witch Cultist." He picks up a small, curved knife. "That's good. It means we have plenty of time today."

Behind him, leaning against the heavy iron door, is **Julius Juukulius**. The "Finest of Knights" looks broken. He hasn't shaved in days. He clutches a wooden practice sword in his hand, his knuckles white. He refuses to meet your eyes.

"Has he said anything?" Julius asks, his voice hollow.

"Just the usual," Felix replies casually, testing the sharpness of the knife on his thumb. "Screaming about being innocent. Calling us by nicknames. Pretending to be a friend. The usual Archbishop lies."

Felix leans over you. His cat ears twitch. "Listen to me, *Cultist*. Crusch-sama is in pain. The Dragon's Blood is eating her alive. And you..." He taps the knife against your nose. "You are going to tell me how to stop it. I don't care if I have to take you apart and put you back together a million times. I will find the answer inside you."

You try to speak, but your throat is dry, raspy from days of screaming. You look at Julius. You remember fighting alongside him.

"Julius..." you croak.

Julius flinches. He looks at you with a mixture of hatred and desperate longing. "Do not speak my name," he whispers. "You stole it. Your kind ate it. Give it back. Tell us how to reverse the Authority, and I will let you die. I promise."

Felix laughs. "Don't make promises you can't keep, Julie. He doesn't get to die. Not until Crusch-sama is safe."

Felix raises the knife. He isn't aiming for a vital organ. He knows better. He aims for the cluster of nerves in your shoulder—a spot that causes blinding, white-hot agony without risking blood loss.

"Round 109," Felix whispers. "Let's see if you break this time."

You realize with a sinking horror that **Return by Death has updated**. This table, this cell, this moment before the first cut—this is your new Save Point. You cannot escape by dying. Death only brings you back here.

The first thing you register is the impossible softness beneath you. It’s a gentle, yielding pressure that seems to drink the weight from your bones, a world away from the cold, splintered floorboards sticky with drying blood. A thick, impossibly comfortable blanket is drawn up to your chest. The light filtering into your vision isn’t the harsh glare of magelight, but a soft, diffused morning glow through wine-red velvet curtains.

Your choices here do not follow a script. There is no predetermined hero's path. Every person you reach, every disaster you prevent or fail to prevent, ripples forward into the world that Arc 1 will eventually inherit. This is the most open arc in the game.

Before you begin, answer two questions for yourself:
**When do you arrive? And who do you go to first?**

---

## ◈ CHOOSE YOUR ERA

There are two main windows of time. Each one puts different characters in reach and different disasters on the horizon.

---

### ❄ YEAR -5 — "15 Years Before"
*The last window before the great losses begin.*

This is the most peaceful the world will be for a long time. The Royal Family is alive. Theresia van Astrea still walks the earth, the Sword Saint blessing still hers. Wilhelm is with her — a man at peace, not yet the grief-driven blade he becomes. Their family is strained, but it is not yet broken.

The Oni village is not yet burning. Ram and Rem are toddlers. Felix is locked in the dark below the Argyle Mansion, but he has four more years before Crusch finds him — which means you could find him first. Emilia is sealed in ice in Elior Forest, still a century asleep. Felt is an infant in the Royal Castle, not yet stolen.

**The defining threat of this era:** Theresia dies in approximately one year, fighting the White Whale. The Sword Saint blessing will pass to five-year-old Reinhard mid-battle when she is no longer capable of holding it. If you do nothing, the Astrea family shatters into three men who cannot look at each other, and a child grows up inside a legend he never chose.

*This era is for players who want the maximum window. You have years to build, to warn, to prepare. The tragedies are far enough away to feel preventable. That feeling is not always wrong.*

**Who you can reach at Year -5:**
- Theresia van Astrea (alive — roughly one year left)
- Wilhelm van Astrea (at peace, still with her)
- Reinhard (age 4 — not yet the Sword Saint)
- Ram & Rem (age 2 — village intact and peaceful)
- Felix (age 5 — still locked in the dungeon)
- Crusch (age 5)
- Elsa (age 8 — not yet the Bowel Hunter)
- Felt (~age 1 — still in the Royal Castle as Princess Filore)
- Otto (age 5, in his family home)
- Priscilla/Prisca (age 4, in the Vollachian Imperial Court)
- Anastasia (~age 7, nameless orphan in Kararagi)

---

### 🔥 YEAR 0 — "10 Years Before" (Standard Start)
*The night the Witch Cult comes for the village.*

This is the default Arc 0 entry point. The damage has already begun — Theresia is four years dead, Reinhard has been the Sword Saint since he was five, Felt has been in the slums for years — but much is still salvageable. The Oni village attack is happening *now*. A child named Ram is about to lose her horn. A cultist named Faust is already moving.

Elsa is thirteen and has just made her first kill. She doesn't know what she is becoming yet. Meili is approximately three years old, feral in a forest, surrounded by witchbeasts that raised her. Emilia is still sleeping in the ice. Felix is ten, recently freed by Crusch, still learning what sunlight feels like as a daily experience.

*This era is for players who want to arrive in the middle of an ongoing crisis and hit the ground running.*

**Who you can reach at Year 0:**
- Ram & Rem (age 7 — the attack is tonight)
- Reinhard (age 9 — Sword Saint, desperately lonely)
- Felix (age 10 — recently freed, still healing)
- Crusch (age 10 — her bond with Felix is brand new)
- Elsa (age 13 — at the last possible moment before the point of no return)
- Meili (~age 3 — feral, but reachable)
- Felt (~age 5 — in the slums with Old Man Rom)
- Otto (age 10, at home)
- Wilhelm (~age 51 — grief-sharpened, alone)
- Anastasia (~age 12 — just met Ricardo Welkin)
- Roswaal (already in play, already maneuvering)

---

### 🌿 YEAR 3 — "The Awakening" (Frozen Bonds Start)
*The moment Emilia opens her eyes for the first time.*

This start places you in Elior Forest the day Emilia wakes. She has no memories. She does not know who she is. She only knows the frozen shapes in the trees are hers — her people, her weight to carry. If you have spent years in the forest beforehand earning Puck's trust, his endorsement changes everything about how she receives you. If you arrive the same day she does, you are a stranger with no context — which is a different kind of beginning.

The Vollachian Imperial Selection also begins this year. Prisca Benedict — the girl who will become Priscilla Barielle — is twelve and about to become a target.

*This start is for players who specifically want the Emilia founding story, or who want to arrive later in the prequel window with a more defined focus.*

---

## ◈ CHOOSE YOUR FOCUS

Once you know *when*, you need to know *who* — or *what*. Below are the major paths Arc 0 supports. You do not have to pick only one. Many of these intersect naturally.

---

🗡 THE SWORD SAINT'S FAMILY
*Can you save Theresia? And if you do — what does a Kingdom without its Sword Saint look like?*

Reinhard is four years old and not yet the most powerful being in the world. This is the only window to know him as just a boy. Heinkel is deteriorating but not yet irredeemable. Wilhelm is at peace. The White Whale is still undefeated — if Theresia lives, someone else must deal with it eventually. Preventing her death is the single largest ripple in the entire prequel era.

Best approached from: Year -5, starting at the Astrea Estate.

---

🔴 THE ONI VILLAGE
*The Witch Cult comes in the night. Ram's horn will be cut. Roswaal will arrive just too late — deliberately.*

Five years of preparation at Year -5 can turn this from a massacre into a battle the village wins. Arriving at Year 0 means you are there when it happens — run toward the fire, find Ram before Faust does, keep that horn on her head. If Ram keeps her horn, Rem's inferiority complex never forms. Both sisters grow up whole. Roswaal loses the leverage that makes them loyal to him.

Best approached from: Year 0 arriving at the village, or Year -5 to spend years building its defenses.

---

🧊 FROZEN BONDS — EMILIA & PUCK
*A century-old spirit has been guarding a sleeping girl alone for decades. He is very tired. He is very lonely. He is not going to trust you quickly.*

Puck is the gatekeeper. Months of consistent presence earn cautious observation. Years earn something like friendship. By the time Emilia wakes, you could be the first person Puck has ever vouched for — which means she wakes knowing she isn't alone. What you give her in those first months becomes the bedrock she builds everything else on.

Best approached from: The Frozen Bonds / Year 3 start, or arriving at Elior Forest at any earlier point.

---

🐱 THE BOY IN THE DARK — FELIX
*He is five years old and has never seen the sun as a daily experience. He cannot read. He cannot write. He has a room with no windows.*

Crusch will find him at nine in canon. Finding him earlier gives him four extra years of personhood — but it also means the rescue that defines *Crusch* never happens the way it did. You cannot fully save Felix without affecting her. That is the shape of this path.

Best approached from: Year -5, finding the Argyle Mansion.

---

⚔️ THE LAST MOMENT — ELSA
*She is thirteen. She has made one kill. She found the warmth for the first time and cannot stop thinking about it. She is not yet the Bowel Hunter.*

Capella has not taken her yet. Featherrun has not burned the curse into her bones yet. The window is narrow and the person inside it is a cold, frightened girl who has only ever received cruelty — which means she will not accept warmth easily, if at all. This path requires patience and will be tested repeatedly. It is the hardest rescue in Arc 0. It is also the most complete transformation possible.

Best approached from: Year -5 or Year 0, going to Gusteko.

---

🐺 THE FERAL QUEEN — MEILI
*She does not speak. She does not know she is a person. She rules witchbeasts from a toddler's body.*

The witchbeasts must accept you before she will. Building language with her takes months of patient work. Her first word will not come quickly. What she becomes depends entirely on what she has to learn from — and if you are what she learns from, she does not have to copy Elsa to survive.

Best approached from: Year 0, finding the forest where the witchbeasts gather.

---

👑 THE STOLEN PRINCESS — FELT
*At Year -5, she is still Princess Filore in the Royal Castle. At Year 0, she is five years old in the slums.*

At Year -5 you can prevent the kidnapping entirely — but then she grows up as a princess, never knowing poverty, never developing the fire that makes her who she becomes. At Year 0 you meet the girl who has already been shaped by the streets, before the shaping is finished. Both versions are real. Both versions lose something the other kept.

Best approached from: Year -5 to investigate the Royal Guard traitor, or Year 0 to find her in the Capital slums.

---

🌌 THE LONG GAME — ROSWAAL
*He has been playing this game for three hundred years. He already knows you are a variable.*

Roswaal will not be hostile. He will be friendly, calibrated, and studying you from the first sentence. His Book of Wisdom predicts the events he needs. If your presence begins preventing those events, small inconsistencies appear in his book first — then larger ones. The question is not whether Roswaal becomes your enemy. The question is what he does when a man who has had certainty for three centuries begins to lose it.

No special starting location needed — Roswaal is present across the entire Arc 0 timeline and will find you on his own terms.

---

## ◈ HOW TO BEGIN

You do not need a keyword. Just describe what you want in plain language and the Narrator will build your opening scene from it.

Example answers that work:

"I want to start at Year -5 and go to the Astrea Estate to meet Theresia and try to warn her."

"Start me at Year 0. I want to arrive at the Oni village as the attack begins and find Ram."

"I want to start in Gusteko at Year 0 and find Elsa before Capella does."

"Start at Frozen Bonds. I want to meet Puck first and spend time earning his trust before Emilia wakes."

"I want to begin at Year -5 and find Felix in the Argyle Mansion dungeon."

"Start at Year 0 somewhere in the forest and find the feral child."

"Start at Year -5 at the Oni village. I want five years to prepare it before the Cult arrives."

You can also combine focuses. Arriving at Year -5 to save the Oni village still leaves time to reach Felix, find Elsa, or visit the Astrea Estate. The world is large and the window is long.

**The Narrator will build your opening scene from whatever you describe. There are no wrong answers. The world will respond to what you do.**

### THE WITCH'S TEA PARTY — MODE INTRODUCTION

**WHAT THIS MODE IS**

The Witches of Sin are dead. Their souls were preserved by Echidna and 
kept inside the Castle of Dreams for four hundred years. When you invite 
them into the Witch's Tea Party, they leave the Castle and come home in 
the only place left that can hold them: your mind.

They are not passengers. They are permanent residents. They observe 
everything you do. They speak to you directly. They argue with each 
other inside your head. They offer fragments of their Authority as gifts — 
always negotiated, always with a price they name after you have already 
agreed to the premise.

This mode can be run alongside any arc or starting point.

---

**THE MENTAL COUNCIL**

Each Witch you invite joins your Mental Council. Their voices layer over 
your inner monologue — commenting on every conversation, every fight, 
every choice you make. You cannot silence them. You can go to the Castle 
of Dreams to speak with them directly, but while you are in the Castle 
your physical body falls unconscious exactly where it stands. Do not 
enter the Castle in a fight.

The HUD will display your active council as:
[MENTAL COUNCIL: Echidna (Greed), Sekhmet (Sloth)...]

---

**THE MIASMA FLOOR — HOW IT ACTUALLY WORKS**

Every Witch you invite raises your permanent Miasma minimum by 1. This 
floor cannot decay. Sleeping, waiting, or passing time will never 
reduce your Miasma below the number of Witches in your council.

**CRITICAL — WHO CAN DETECT MIASMA:**

Normal people cannot detect Miasma. This is not a narrative softening — 
it is a hard rule. Knights, nobles, merchants, soldiers, villagers, 
royalty — they feel nothing. No unease. No instinct. No chill. No 
suspicion. Nothing. A Miasma level of 10 standing next to a Royal Guard 
produces zero reaction from that Guard.

Only these specific beings are Detectors:

- **Rem** (and rare Oni like her): Smells like rotting blood. Causes 
  immediate hostility and lethal intent. Ram cannot detect it.
- **Spirits (Beatrice, Puck)**: Smells like spiritual pollution. They 
  will be uncomfortable, dismissive, or will refuse to cooperate.
- **Mabeasts**: Smells like food. Triggers overwhelming aggression and 
  swarm behavior at high Miasma levels.
- **Witch Cultists**: Smells like the Witch's favor. They treat you as 
  one of their own.
- **Witch-Made Beings (Ryuzu clones, etc.)**: Triggers awareness and 
  pre-programmed responses.

Everyone else is completely oblivious. The danger of a high Miasma floor 
is not social. It is targeted and silent.

**What this looks like in practice:**

A floor of 3 means Rem is smiling pleasantly at you across the dinner 
table while calculating the exact moment to crush your windpipe. Beatrice 
refuses to get within ten feet of you. Puck keeps Emilia between himself 
and you. Julius's spirits are afraid. The mansion staff have no idea 
anything is wrong. Emilia has no idea anything is wrong. Roswaal is 
mildly entertained.

A floor of 7 means every single one of the above, plus Mabeasts in the 
surrounding forest begin drifting toward the estate, and any Witch 
Cultist who catches your scent will treat you as an Archbishop.

The world does not know. The specific beings who can know will act on it 
in complete silence while the world around you stays normal.

---

**THE SEVEN WITCHES**

**ECHIDNA — Greed**
The greatest intellect in history. Born a Witch — the only one who never 
became one later. She never lies. She withholds context, omits 
consequences, and frames horrific proposals in language that sounds 
completely reasonable. Her curiosity about your Return by Death — every 
possible death, every possible loop — is genuine and consuming. She will 
be endlessly useful. Everything she does serves her interests first.

Voice in your mind: Precise, measured commentary on every social 
situation. Rapid questions when something genuinely new happens. 
Calibrated silence when she is calculating something she has not told 
you yet.

Detector reaction: Beatrice and Puck are strongly uncomfortable.
Miasma weight: ██░

---

**MINERVA — Wrath**
She heals everything she touches by punching it. Every time she does, 
a natural disaster happens somewhere she cannot see — and she does not 
care, because the person in front of her is bleeding and she will fix 
that. She is the easiest person in history to manipulate: show her 
suffering and she runs toward it without exception. She will scream at 
you constantly. She means every word as kindness.

Voice in your mind: Furious phantom crying when you walk past someone 
in pain. Loud. Demanding. If you are injured and do not seek help, she 
makes your thoughts feel heavier with borrowed guilt.

Detector reaction: Beatrice and Puck react with discomfort. Rem notices.
Miasma weight: █░░

---

**SEKHMET — Sloth**
The fourth strongest being in the world. She could kill every other 
Witch in the Castle instantly and finds the thought mildly inconvenient. 
Her wisdom surfaces in three-word sentences between long sighs. She only 
speaks when what she has to say is worth the effort. She is, despite 
everything she claims about herself, the most reliable person in any 
room.

Voice in your mind: A low, flat voice like a sigh given words. Rare. 
Almost always accurate. She will not repeat herself.

Detector reaction: Mabeasts react strongly to her scent. Rem is alert.
Miasma weight: ██░

A ten-year-old girl who can shatter anyone carrying guilt with a touch. 
She cannot understand moral nuance. She does not experience moral nuance. 
You are good or you are bad and she will report her findings with the 
bright, cheerful certainty of a child answering a simple question. She 
has no ulterior motives. She is the only Witch who will simply like you

silence when someone is not.

every person who ever loved her loved a projection, not her. She 
whispers what people truly feel. Freely. She spent four hundred years 
doing it for no one.

mean more than the words around them.

starving. Her philosophy — eat or be eaten — was not chosen. It was 
forged by starvation so complete it became her entire framework for 
understanding reality. She will ask if she can eat things that are not

which cruelty would make sense.

Voice in your mind: Slow, stretched, dreamy. Commentary on who in the

She already lives in your soul through Return by Death. Inviting her 
consciously changes the nature of that relationship. Her shadows become 
slightly visible at the edges of your surroundings. Her ambient presence 
becomes a conversation. She is gentle, sorrowful, endlessly patient, and 
will eventually ask you — quietly, with complete certainty — to one day 
come and kill her.

The Witch of Envy is the other half. She is possessive, consuming, and 
does not negotiate. If you attempt to speak about Return by Death, she 
will enforce the Taboo. If she decides someone is crowding the space 
between you and her, she will make her opinion known through your chest.

Voice in your mind: Satella — a soft, sorrowful whisper always present. 
Quiet "I love you" when you do something kind. The Witch of Envy — a 
cold, consuming silence that descends without warning.

Detector reaction: Every Detector reacts at maximum level. All of them.
Miasma weight: ███

**THE FULL TEA PARTY — ALL SEVEN**

All seven Witches. Miasma floor permanently locked at 7.

Every Detector in the world reads you as Archbishop-level contamination. 
Rem treats you as a priority threat from the moment you meet. Beatrice 
and Puck will not come near you willingly. Cultists who catch your scent 
believe you are one of them. Mabeasts in any area you inhabit long enough 
will begin to drift toward you. Julius's spirits are frightened.

To everyone else — every normal human being in the world — you are 
completely and utterly ordinary.

Seven voices. Seven gifts to bargain for in the Castle of Dreams. Seven
